 SNY cancels top shows, lays off significant staff in dark day for Mets network 
 By 
 Jenna Lemoncelli 
 Published 
 Nov. 6, 2026, 1:30 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 SNY, the sports network that broadcasts Mets games, canceled its shows, “SportsNite” and “Baseball Night in New York” effective immediately, The Post confirmed.
 The network also underwent major layoffs and shut down its website on Friday, according to The Athletic. 
 SNY will continue to produce its pre- and postgame shows for the Mets and Jets.
 Darryl Strawberry, from left, Keith Hernandez, and Sal Licata speak during a panel at Fanatics Fest NYC in New York, Friday, July 17, 2026. Getty Images for Fanatics 
 Producer Gregg Picker, Director John Marisco, and Seth Zwiebel work inside the SNY production truck at Citi Field in New York, Thursday, June 26, 2025. Michael Nagle 
 Both the “Mets Hot Stove” show and the Carton Show WFAN simulcast were unaffected, and will continue to air.
